AMGN.rationale: Amgen presents a deteriorating fundamental picture masked by surface-level valuation attractiveness. The PE of 26.1x appears cheap versus its 1-year range (22.6x–49.7x), but this compression is earnings-driven (Q1 2026 GAAP EPS of $3.34 vs. $3.20 YoY) rather than a market dislocation — the stock has risen 32.6% over the period. The earnings yield of 3.8% offers no premium over the 4.49% 10-year Treasury, removing any valuation cushion. Quarterly earnings are volatile (2.2x spread between lowest and highest EPS), and the TTM data is incomplete due to a fiscal gap, preventing reliable normalization. The Corlanor recall (935K bottles, Class II) and the $10.7B IRS tax dispute add further downside risk. While the Enbrel pricing injunction and Repatha data are modest positives, they do not offset the structural erosion of the legacy franchise. MariTide in obesity faces entrenched competition from Lilly and Novo Nordisk with no proven efficacy advantage. On balance, all three pillars point negative: deteriorating fundamentals from patent cliffs and regulatory crises, no valuation safety margin versus risk-free rates, and no credible near-term catalyst to reverse the trajectory.
